findings.source_quote: habes ergo eas adiutrices, quo magis possis huius mandata servare
findings.english_quote: They will help you keep his commandments.
findings.issue: The simplified sentence omits the comparative force of magis: the helpers enable him to keep the commandments more effectively. It also replaces his present possession of these helpers with a future statement about their help. The standard edition preserves both features, but the simplified edition does not independently cover them.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “So you have them as helpers, so that you can better keep his commandments.” Review the proposed wording afresh before adoption.

findings.source_quote: illae vero haec verba libenter audierunt.
findings.english_quote: Shorten sentences while preserving virgins, purity, the source’s life/exclusion warning, duties to people in need and the final departure.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata attributes content to this selected unit that it does not contain. There are no duties to people in need here, and the unit ends with the virgins gladly hearing the instructions, not a final departure. Their conditional departure from a defiled house is a different assertion. This is an inaccurate account of the source coverage, even though those additional events have not been inserted into the reader text.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the references to duties to people in need and the final departure. Describe this unit’s actual content, including the helpers, commandments, purity conditions, entrustment, and the virgins’ willing reception of the instructions.

summary: The standard edition faithfully covers the selected working source, including its categorical necessity and exclusion language. Its bounded choice of “I know” is adequately disclosed against Latin “I see” and supported as a reported reading by the supplied evidence; the purity alternative is distinguished from the retained Latin dwelling wording and editorial reconstruction. The simplified edition needs restoration of the helpers clause’s comparative and present force, and correction of its inaccurate scope metadata. This review evaluates the supplied texts and attributed reports, not unseen manuscript images or exhaustive witness collation.
